plan.contextChunk: This figure lays out a multichannel convolution as one symbolic equation joining three groups of tensors drawn in offset perspective. On the left, under the bold label w, sit two stacks of light blue square grids, each three sheets deep; a tall brace at the far left reads C_out filters and spans both stacks, a small brace above the upper stack reads C_in, and braces along the right side and the bottom edge of the lower stack each read K for the filter's two spatial extents. A star operator separates the filter bank from the middle group, labeled x_in, a much larger pink grid also drawn as three offset sheets, with a brace above reading C_in and a brace beneath its width reading M. An equals sign leads to the right-hand group, labeled x_out, a single pink grid whose upper brace reads C_out and whose right-hand brace reads N. Color keeps the learned parameters distinct from the data, and the braces let the reader match dimensions straight across the operator: the filter bank's depth agrees with the input's C_in, while the number of filters becomes the output's C_out. The drawing spells out shape bookkeeping that is easy to lose track of in symbols alone.

interactions.label: C_out filters
interactions.teaches: Each blue filter stack produces exactly one output channel, so changing C_out changes both the number of learned filters and the number of sheets in x_out together

interactions.label: Kernel size K
interactions.teaches: K controls only the spatial footprint of each filter and the matching receptive patch on x_in, while the full input width M remains larger and fixed

demo_steps.title: Default multichannel convolution
demo_steps.narration: Two blue filter stacks are shown, and the output tensor has two matching pink sheets. Each filter stack spans all C_in input channels but covers only a K by K spatial patch.

demo_steps.title: More output channels
demo_steps.narration: Increasing C_out adds more blue filter stacks and the output gains the same number of sheets. This makes the one-filter-to-one-output-channel relationship explicit.

demo_steps.title: Larger spatial kernel
demo_steps.narration: Increasing K enlarges the blue grids and the highlighted receptive patch on x_in, but the input tensor still spans M by M cells. The kernel is local in space but full-depth across C_in.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique symbolic tensor drawing: front faces are true axis-aligned square grids, with +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, and +Z receding diagonally up-left. One grid cell is about 0.28 world units. Fixed C_in = 3 sheets for both the filter stacks and x_in. Fixed input spatial size M = 7 cells, so x_in front face is 1.96 × 1.96 world units in X × Y, with Z depth equal to 3 sheets using an offset of about (-0.18, +0.12) world units per sheet. Filter stacks have variable spatial size K × K cells: at default K = 3 each blue front face is 0.84 × 0.84 world units; at K = 5 it is 1.40 × 1.40. Each filter stack has depth C_in = 3 along +Z, so every filter is K × K × 3. Arrange the C_out filter stacks in one vertical column at the left, centered around x ≈ -3.7; default C_out = 2 with one stack above and one below, matching the source. If C_out changes, distribute stacks vertically with even spacing, keeping the large left brace spanning all stacks. The input tensor sits in the middle at x ≈ 0, larger than the filters. The output tensor sits at x ≈ +3.9 and has fixed spatial size N = 7 cells for visual correspondence with the source, so each output sheet is 1.96 × 1.96 world units; its depth equals C_out sheets along the same up-left receding direction. The receptive patch highlight lies on the front sheet of x_in, anchored near the upper-left interior of the grid, and covers exactly K × K input cells. Dominant colors: filters light blue #cfe8f6, data/output pale pink #f4d7d4, grid/braces/operators/text black #111111, receptive patch translucent amber #f6c44f at about 35% opacity with a darker orange outline #d98c00. Keep the symbolic equation layout left-to-right: filter bank, star, x_in, equals sign, x_out. Labels are black bold serif math style: w, x_in, x_out; dimension labels C_out filters, C_in, K, M, C_out, and N.
interactionPlan.notes: Render each sheet as a filled plane with separate black LineSegments for grid lines so K and M can update cleanly. Use an orthographic camera and explicit oblique offsets rather than perspective shrinking. Draw rear sheets first and front sheets last for correct stacking. Curly braces can be SVG/SDF text curves or billboarded 2D overlays pinned to world positions. Slider changes should animate sheet insertion/removal and grid resizing over about 250 ms to preserve the shape correspondence.

discrepancies: The tensor layer depth appears to recede down/right in the generated input and output stacks, whereas the source layers recede up/left behind the front sheet.
An amber receptive-field patch is added on x_in, which is not present in the source figure.
The large left C_out filters delimiter is a thick curly brace that overlaps the filter stacks, while the source uses a cleaner outside bracket/parenthesis-like delimiter.
Several brace annotations, especially C_in and C_out, are positioned too close to the stacks and look less like the source layout.
The generated figure is more compressed and leaves the main equation smaller relative to the canvas because of the added control panel.
evaluation.notes: The main convolution tensor equation is recognizable and mostly complete, but the depth direction, extra receptive-field highlight, and some brace placements reduce fidelity.
action_items: Reverse or adjust the layer offsets/projection so all stacks visually recede up-left as in the source figure.
Remove the amber receptive-field patch from the default view, or hide it behind an optional interaction step.
Move the C_out filters brace and vertical label farther left so they do not overlap the blue filter stacks.
Tune the C_in, C_out, K, M, and N brace positions and sizes to more closely match the source annotation layout.
